fighterA.name: Jiren

dossier.style: Ultra-efficient fighting of pure strength and Ki. He relies on minimal movement and devastating counters that end the fight before the opponent can react.
dossier.advantage: Overwhelming energy barrier and reflexes. His Ki is so powerful that it serves as both an impenetrable defense and the ultimate offense.
dossier.mentality: A stoic absolutist. He fights without unnecessary words or emotions, taking the shortest path to total dominance over the opponent.
dossier.quote: It matters not how many weaklings band together. You are nothing before absolute strength.

powers: Extreme ki output, barrier techniques and elite speed/reactions.
weaknesses: Limited utility compared with heavy hax specialists.

crucialFeats: Tags UI Goku a few times.
No sells a Kamehameha from SSB Goku.
Detects and Counters attacks coming from a different dimension.
Is more powerful than his universe God of Destruction.

fighterB.name: Saitama

dossier.style: Simple, direct punch attacks. His style relies on such massive physical superiority that technique becomes redundant for him.
dossier.advantage: Immeasurable strength and resilience. He has no limits – every strike has finishing potential, and he remains immune to most attacks.
dossier.mentality: A bored and carefree professional. He doesn't take the fight seriously until someone forces him to exert effort, which he waits for with hope.
dossier.quote: 100 push-ups, 100 sit-ups, 100 squats, and a 10km run EVERY SINGLE DAY!!!

powers: Extreme physical power, durability, stamina, and growth under prolonged conflict.
tools: Direct close-range offense and rapid adaptation through the fight.
weaknesses: Minimal formal technique variety. Relies heavily on direct engagement.

crucialFeats: Serious Punch Squared carves a void through space.
Saitama time travels to reverse causality.
A Serious Sneeze blows away the gas surrounding Jupiter's.

tactical-board.headline: TACTICAL BOARD // JIREN VS SAITAMA
tactical-board.subtitle: Discipline versus Limitlessness
tactical-board.lane: Jiren wins by ending the early fight. Saitama wins by surviving long enough to make the early fight irrelevant.

final-summary.headline: FINAL SUMMARY
final-summary.subtitle: Summary
final-summary.winner: Jiren leads, but Saitama has a live late branch
final-summary.line1: Jiren owns the paper comparison, 89.67 vs 81.22.
final-summary.line2: Jiren's baseline comes from better opening control and cleaner finish structure.
final-summary.line3: Saitama only flips the matchup if survival turns into real escalation and the anomaly branch becomes live.

battle-dynamics.headline: BATTLE DYNAMICS
battle-dynamics.subtitle: How the fight changes minute by minute.
battle-dynamics.phase1: Jiren starts high because pressure, barriers, and clean reads matter most early.
battle-dynamics.phase2: Saitama's line rises only if the first real finish does not stick.
battle-dynamics.phase3: Jiren loses leverage fast once the fight crosses from opening control into late escalation.
battle-dynamics.analysis: Jiren wins the cleaner start. Saitama wins the messier future version.

x-factor.headline: X-FACTOR
x-factor.subtitle: The variable that affects the verdict more than ordinary stats.
x-factor.mechanika: Jiren's edge lives in the first clean finish window. Saitama's edge appears only if that window fails badly enough.
x-factor.implikacja: If Jiren keeps the fight early, he wins cleanly. If the fight slips, Saitama becomes the more dangerous future engine.
x-factor.psychologia: Jiren wants the fight solved before it becomes strange. Saitama only needs enough fight to let strange happen.

interpretation.headline: INTERPRETATION
interpretation.subtitle: Who wins the fight on paper?
interpretation.line1: Jiren owns the better start, cleaner reads, and more reliable opening finish structure.
interpretation.line2: Saitama keeps a real late branch only because his survivability can turn the future version of the fight into something worse.
interpretation.line3: On paper the edge is Jiren's, but the fight stops being a paper fight if survival turns into escalation.
interpretation.quote: The start belongs to Jiren. The danger belongs to whatever survives it.

fight-simulation.headline: FIGHT SIMULATION
fight-simulation.subtitle: The course of the fight across three phases.
fight-simulation.opening: Jiren takes immediate control through pressure, spacing, and efficiency.
fight-simulation.midFight: Saitama survives rather than dictates and tries to stay alive long enough for the exchange to change.
fight-simulation.lateFight: The fight diverges based on whether Jiren closes early or Saitama survives into escalation.
fight-simulation.endCondition: Jiren wins by ending the first version of the fight. Saitama wins by surviving into a stronger second version.

stat-trap.headline: STAT TRAP
stat-trap.subtitle: Why better stats do not guarantee victory
stat-trap.trapTop: OPENING EDGE DECIDES THE FIRST VERSION OF THE FIGHT
stat-trap.trapBottom: ESCALATION CAN CREATE A WORSE SECOND VERSION
stat-trap.example: Jiren can control the start and still lose the later exchange if the first finish never truly happens.
stat-trap.question: Can Jiren finish before survival turns into escalation?
